problem: Let $u$ and $v$ be vectors such that $‖u‖=6\sqrt{2}$ and $‖u+2v‖=6\sqrt{6}.$  If $u$ is orthogonal to $v$, find $‖v‖.$

feedback.problem: Let $u$ and $v$ be vectors such that $‖u‖=4$ and $‖\sqrt{2}u+\sqrt{3}v‖=\sqrt{182}.$  If $u$ is orthogonal to $v$, find $‖v‖.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $u$ is orthogonal to $v,$ we also have that $\sqrt{2}u$ is orthogonal to $\sqrt{3}v.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem states that

$$
\begin{aligned}‖\sqrt{2}u+\sqrt{3}v{‖}^{2} & =‖\sqrt{2}u{‖}^{2}+‖\sqrt{3}v{‖}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Simplifying and substituting in the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖\sqrt{2}u+\sqrt{3}v{‖}^{2} & =(\sqrt{2}‖u‖)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}‖v‖)^{2} \\ ‖\sqrt{2}u+\sqrt{3}v{‖}^{2} & =2‖u{‖}^{2}+3‖v{‖}^{2} \\ (\sqrt{182})^{2} & =2(4)^{2}+3‖v{‖}^{2} \\ 182 & =2\cdot 16+3‖v{‖}^{2} \\ 182 & =32+3‖v{‖}^{2} \\ 150 & =3‖v{‖}^{2} \\ ‖v{‖}^{2} & =50\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $‖v‖=5\sqrt{2}.$
